Tl;dnr: Ducking awesome!

Easy to get into, flexible and broad gameplay, totally worth the money. This is exactly what I was hoping to get from an indie-team as a single-player experience. If this ever gets native co-op, this might go through the roof!

This game supports nearly all the gameplay-loops you are looking for in an extraction-shooter: Day/Night cycles with additional hazards, clear designed maps with an endless way to interact with the elements, fluid gunplay that steps beyond the isometric standards. 

After all the hours put into the game on "relaxed" difficulty I find myself pumping the difficulty to higher steps because I enjoy the challenge. If you take the time to read the quests and are willing to put in a little grind, you will see that every minute you put into it gets rewarded. 

I can not keep stressing how good the gun-game feels: even as a visually impaired person, I never struggle to make out the targets and it gives easy to read visuals. The gun statistics make sense, are listed in a logical way and use numbers that translate directly to the feeling when you press the mouse button.
Even without additional mods, there are an endless amount of playstyles supported for you CQB and tactic fanatics: Stealth sniper, LMG tank, SMG-runner or even melee-rambo is not only possible but is supported by the options you get with classes, totems, weight and armor balance and different ammo types. 

I am stunned to see what a small team of developers can put on their flappy feet, special thanks for the translators making it possible to let more enjoy this gem! Can't wait to see how this game develops, so far the regular updates and smart changes makes me really believe in indies from the other side of the globe!

This is unironically one of the most fun games I have ever played. It also has a mind-boggling amount of content. Now, maybe my expectations were lower because I came in thinking this was a meme game, but the feeling I had when I reached the third zone and opened the map for the first time can only be compared to Elden Ring - that "oh my god there's MORE?" feeling. On top of that, the controls are tight, the visibility/aiming/recoil systems are great and pretty intuitive, and the UI and inventory systems are good. Not perfect - I understand storage space is part of the progression, but I feel like the rules on what can and can't stack, as well as stack sizes, could be tweaked some more. Maybe different stack rules for backpack vs warehouse? Especially for food. "I need to increase my storage for all the cool attachments I have" feels much better than "I need to increase my storage because my soda cans take up a whole slot each and I feel dumb selling them for pennies when I extract with them by accident". Regardless, phenomenal game, devs cooked big time (and not by getting lucky, either, it's very obvious a lot of thought went into many of the things that make this game good). 9/10.

Yeah this is fun. Some UI issues dealing with inventory, somewhat helped by some of the top mods, but the combat and shoot and loot loop is excellently done.

Kinda wish there was more funny stuff that you could do with some of the items (like microphone or radio) and it doesn't really seem like default difficulty makes crafting anything all that worthwhile unless you need it for an upgrade because the loot is just thrown at you, but still the whole package is fun as hell.

It's honestly been really fun so far. The quality is unexpectedly good, and the performance is too. I have found some of the writing to be pretty funny, but sometimes it does seem like it's trying too hard to be funny (besides the character creation, which is honestly hilarious and good).

Basically though, it's a single-player top-down extraction shooter, which is more addicting than others I've played due to a lack of procedural generation, and having lore to collect and learn. Maps aren't just flat grids with buildings strewn about randomly, but are actually hand-crafted with only loot and container locations being *mostly* randomized. A lot of the mechanics are pretty solid, and really the only frustration thus far has been that the warehouse storage is *never* big enough for me, you can expand it, and use the loot you've gathered; but I am one to grab everything "just in case" and it usually comes back to haunt me later. lol

My ONLY gripes are that:
There's no co-op,
And there's no native controller support (so steam deck support is quite limited :( ).
Otherwise I've had no technical issues at all.

Overall I do recommend this game, it's charming and addicting and sets a good example for future top-down extraction-shooter releases. The price isn't half bad either, and it's optimized better than a large number of games that have similar art-styles.

This is how you make an extraction shooter!

Although the graphics might look cartoony, underneath sits a fun and engaging extraction shooter, PvE only that is! The graphics are crisp and the customisation of your character fun to do. You can do quests to expand your base and scavange various locations for loot and resources. every map has a set location of extract points and progressing your base you can have a teleporter to (randomly) spawn in one of the maps instead of going for the walk.

Every location has one or more boss enemies, which all have different attacking patterns. Don't go undergeared to the higher levels! There is a day and night cycle, and you can rest without penalty during the night or day. Night raids are more dangerous as robotic spiders roam the world, in addition to the evil Ducks which are standard available. But some quests and items only drop at night, and so you will have to venture out there in the future.
When you die, you can return to the location to grab the dropped loot. Should you die on the way to it, however, your original lootbag will disappear and replaced with your last one. This makes retrieval missions tense as the enemies respawned and you might have ran low on weapon and ammo reserves. It is wise to have at least one backup loadout stashed in your base for these events.

Your character can be upgraded with different perks on multiple perk trees. Your warehouse space can be expanded too, which is needed especially as you collect more loot. Loot drops are random although some items drop more regularly in certain locations. Some quest items can also be bought from the traders in your base and by completing quests you unlock new craftable items. 

The sound effects are great and directional, and all equipment is shown on your character. You have various gradations of armour (body/head) as well as gasmasks and such. Weapons can be customised with attachments which give less recoil, silenced, etc. 

There are lots of items to gather which you can sell or dismantle. Your base can be upgraded adding workbenches, bitcoin miners, weapon traders etc. 

The Devs said more than 2 million players have bought it which, if it is the case, shows you that this game is well worth your time. It is not ridiciously priced so that too is a plus! I am having great fun and you can easily do a run between chores or on a break at work!
